# swarmops git import

Bring a git repository's history in: every commit --ref reaches that the store does not hold becomes a changeset, parents first, and --into moves to the changeset of --ref's commit, created if it does not exist.

The repository is read on this host, at PATH, relative to the working directory: a work tree, which holds .git, or a bare repository. Each changeset keeps its git commit's id in its git.oid metadata, and its author and committer in its signatures; it records no agent. Run again, it takes only the commits after the one --into's head holds, and writes nothing when that is --ref's commit. A head that holds no git commit, or one --ref does not reach, fails with E\_GIT\_IMPORT\_DIVERGED (exit 3), and nothing is written.

Content a changeset cannot hold as git has it is refused by class (E\_GIT\_IMPORT\_LOSSY, naming the commit, the path and the class) unless --lossy allows that class: then it is dropped or normalized, and the changeset names the class in its git.lossy metadata.

```yaml

description: "Bring a git repository's history in: every commit --ref reaches that the store does not hold, then move --into to it."
group: "git"
since: "0.1.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: true
mcp_tool: ""
envelope_op: "git_import"
exit_codes: [0, 1, 3, 6]
errors: [E_GIT_NOT_A_REPO, E_GIT_REF_NOT_FOUND, E_GIT_IMPORT_DIVERGED, E_GIT_IMPORT_LOSSY, E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED, E_GIT_READ]
syntax: "swarmops git import [OPTIONS] <PATH>"
```

## Syntax

```text
swarmops git import [OPTIONS] <PATH>
```

## Required arguments

### `PATH`

Syntax: `<PATH>`.

The git repository's directory.

## Optional arguments

The command also takes the [global options](../cli.md#global-options).

### `--ref`

Syntax: `--ref <GIT_REF>`.
Default: `HEAD`.

The commit to import, with every commit it reaches: HEAD, a ref's name or a commit id.

### `--into`

Syntax: `--into <REF>`.
Default: `main`.

The ref to move to that commit's changeset: main or release/&lt;name&gt;.

### `--lossy`

Syntax: `--lossy <CLASS>...`.

A class of content to drop or normalize instead of refusing it, or all; repeatable. Values: `gitlinks`: A submodule's entry: dropped; `paths`: A name that is not UTF-8, or is . or ..: dropped; `modes`: A mode git does not write, such as 100664: normalized; `tree_order`: A tree out of git's order, or naming an entry twice: put in order; `empty_trees`: An entry naming an empty tree: dropped; `nonstandard`: A commit whose bytes the changeset cannot keep: kept as its fields hold it; `all`: Every class.

### `--gitlinks`

Syntax: `--gitlinks <WHAT>`.

What to do with a submodule's entry: refuse it, or drop it as --lossy gitlinks does; given, it decides that class whatever --lossy says. Values: `refuse`: Refuse the commit that holds one (E\_GIT\_IMPORT\_LOSSY); `drop`: Drop it, and name the class in the changeset's git.lossy metadata.

## Examples

### CLI

```sh
swarmops --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17 git import [tmp]/missing
```

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "op": "git_import",
  "api": 1,
  "error": {
    "code": "E_GIT_NOT_A_REPO",
    "message": "no git repository it can open there: \"[tmp]/missing\" does not appear to be a git repository: Could not retrieve metadata of \"[tmp]/missing\": No such file or directory (os error 2)",
    "retryable": false,
    "exit": 6,
    "details": {
      "git_path": "[tmp]/missing"
    },
    "hint": null
  },
  "meta": {
    "repo": "[tmp]/store",
    "elapsed_ms": "[elapsed_ms]",
    "resolved": {},
    "auth": "trust"
  }
}
```

Exit code 6. Recorded by the CLI tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time.

## Return information

`result` is a `GitImportResp` (`swarmops schema GitImportResp` prints its JSON Schema).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `git_head_sha` | `string` | yes | `git_ref`'s commit: its git id, 40 lowercase hex digits. |
| `head_changeset` | `string` | yes | The changeset of `git_ref`'s commit, which `target_ref` names now. |
| `imported` | `integer` | yes | How many commits became changesets in this import. |
| `lossy` | `array of LossyCommitOut` | yes | The commits this import took lossily, as the request's `lossy` allowed: the first 100, in the order imported. `lossy_total` counts them all. |
| `lossy_total` | `integer` | yes | How many commits this import took lossily, the ones past the first 100 included. |
| `old_head` | `string or null` | no | What `target_ref` named when the import started; omitted when it did not exist, and the import created it. |
| `ref_moved` | `boolean` | yes | Whether this import moved `target_ref`, or created it; `false` when the ref named `head_changeset` already, after an earlier import of the same commit or a concurrent one. |
| `skipped` | `integer` | yes | How many commits the import found in the store already, where its walk stopped: the commit of the target's head, or commits an earlier import made. Importing the commit the target names already imports 0 and skips 1. |
| `target_ref` | `string` | yes | The ref the import moved, or found at `head_changeset` already. |
| `warnings` | `array of string` | no | Problems the import met that did not stop it, such as failed housekeeping after the target's move became durable; the import itself succeeded. Omitted when empty. |

Envelope `op`: `git_import`.

Exit codes:

- `0`: Success.
- `1`: The operation failed.
- `3`: The change conflicts with what it lands on: resolve it, then run the operation again.
- `6`: Something the request names does not exist.

## Errors

- [`E_GIT_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_git_not_a_repo) (exit 6): `git import` found no git repository it can open at `git_path` (`details.git_path`).
- [`E_GIT_REF_NOT_FOUND`](../errors.md#e_git_ref_not_found) (exit 6): `git import`: the source repository has no `git_ref`, or it names no commit (`details.git_ref`; `details.kind` the object it names instead, such as a tree).
- [`E_GIT_IMPORT_DIVERGED`](../errors.md#e_git_import_diverged) (exit 3): `git import`: the target ref's head is not the import of `git_ref`'s commit or of an ancestor of it, because the source was rewritten or a native changeset was committed on the target, so nothing was written; there is no silent merge.
- [`E_GIT_IMPORT_LOSSY`](../errors.md#e_git_import_lossy) (exit 1): `git import`: a commit holds content a changeset cannot keep as git has it; `details` names the `commit`, the `path` (also as `path_base64` when it is not UTF-8) and the lossy `class`, which the request's `lossy` can allow.
- [`E_GIT_UNSUPPORTED`](../errors.md#e_git_unsupported) (exit 1): `git import` does not read the source: a SHA-256 repository, reftable refs, a shallow clone, a FIFO, a socket or a device where it reads a file of the git directory, a file it reads whole there that is longer than 16 MiB, a commit of more than 255 parents, or an entry whose mode is no kind of entry; `details.reason` says which (`object_format`, `ref_storage`, `shallow`, `special_file`, `file_too_long`, `parents`, `mode`), `details.file` names the file of `special_file` and `file_too_long` by its path in the git directory (`details.size` and `details.max` give the long one's length and the limit), and `details.commit` names the commit of `parents` and `mode`.
- [`E_GIT_READ`](../errors.md#e_git_read) (exit 1): `git import` could not read the source: an object is missing (as in a partial clone), does not hash to its id or does not parse, or the filesystem refused a read (`details.reason`; `details.object` names the object when there is one).

Any command that opens a store may also fail with a store error, such as [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo), [`E_IO`](../errors.md#e_io) or [`E_STORE_CORRUPT`](../errors.md#e_store_corrupt); a command line the grammar refuses is [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg) (exit 2).
